full_judgment:
8; Before entering into discussion on the common questions of law and facts in both the proceedings I think it would be convenient to dispose of the matter relating to the jurisdiction of the Administrative Tribunal to entertain the case of Mr. A.B.M. Hamid Khan. It may be mentioned however that in the pleading the defendants did not raise such a plea that the said plaintiff ought to have gone to the Administrative Tribunal. Their plea as in the case of Md. Shahabuddin was that the remedy lay in the Labour Court. It appears from the judgment of the lower appellate court that the learned Advocate for the Bank raised such a plea there for the first time, and the learned District Judge observing that the Administrative Tribunal (Amendment) Ordinance 1984 having given to the Administrative Tribunal exclusive jurisdiction to entertain the case of the employees of the Janata Bank with effect from 25.9.84, Mr. A.B.M. Hamid Khan who filed his suit in 1985ought to have moved the tribunal for adjudication of the dispute. Mr. Chakraborty has referred to the second proviso to section 4(2) of the Administrative Tribunals Act and argues that the statutory period of6 months limitation having long elapsed before the amendment has been made there was no question ofthe Tribunal entertaining the case in 1985. The other side has not advanced any argument on this point. Itis clear from the Proviso referred to above that the Administrative Tribunal would not entertain any case unless it is filed before it within six months from the date of the impugned order. 

 9. The plaintiffs cause of action arose on 17.9.81 that is 4 years before the Administrative Tribunal got jurisdiction to entertain such a case. The learned District Judge does not appear to have taken notice of the relevant Provision regarding limitation in driving the plaintiffs to the Administrative Tribunal which would not certainly entertain his case after four (4) years. I would therefore, agree with Mr. Chakraborty that the learned District Judge has committed an error of law in finding that the remedy of the plaintiff A.B.M. Hamid Khan lies in the Administrative Tribunal. In such view of the matter the proper forum for both the cases cannot but be one and the same. "
